newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna's Astra stake rises, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna's Astra stake rises, shares fall.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna announced on Tuesday that he effectively controlled the largest single stake in Astra International, Indonesia's largest car manufacturer, but its shares fell after a two-week surge.

Astra fell 50 rupiah (2.2 U.S. cents) to 3,750 as investors were convinced that any further play on the stock as part of a possible takeover bid would be aimed at large shareholders and that small holders would be unlikely to reap any further benefit, business analysts said.
The share has risen from 2,625 rupiah on September 16, when rumours first surfaced that a takeover was in the making.

"We feel that at this level the share is slightly overvalued and there is limited upside," said David Chang, director of research at Vickers Ballas Tamara. "Only today, we recommended a sell on the stock."
Sampoerna, the head of cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna and one of Indonesia's wealthiest men, had said on Monday that he had bought a 9.81 stake in Astra in his individual capacity.
On Tuesday, PT Sampoerna announced that a wholly-owned subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake in Astra.
That would take the stake controlled by Sampoerna to 12.66 percent, the largest single holding in Astra.
But the market remains convinced that members of President Suharto's family were eyeing the company and that Sampoerna could sell his stake to one of them, brokers said.
An Indonesian newspaper has named Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana and his sons Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hutomo Mandala Putra as prospective buyers.
The report has not been independently confirmed.
"If Astra becomes controlled by the first family, it becomes a political stock and becomes subject to the same sort of vulnerability," said one foreign broker.
"The risks would increase quite substantially," the broker added, saying that this could be one of the reasons for Tuesday's fall in Astra share prices.
He added that Suharto's family was likely to approach large shareholders, government banks and state-run pension funds to build up their stakes and that small investors were now out of the picture.
Meanwhile, shares in PT Sampoerna fell 300 rupiah to 22,300 on Tuesday, off a low of 21,800, as Moody's and Standard & Poor's put ratings of its U.S. dollar denominated notes on creditwatch.
Both agencies said the move was triggered by the Astra purchase.

"For the time being, I would like to recommend a hold on Sampoerna until the company gives a full explanation on why they are suddenly investing in the auto industry," said Darmadi Widjaja, an analyst of Sassoon Securities Indonesia.
Widjaja said he would have re-calculate the risk of Sampoerna as its core business was tobacco-related, but now it was also involved in the car industry.
